passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: (dollars in millions, except as noted and per share data) Company Background The Sherwin-Williams Company, founded in 1866, and its consolidated subsidiaries (collectively, the Company) are engaged in the development, manufacture, distribution and sale of paint, coatings and related products to professional, industrial, commercial and retail customers primarily in North and South America with additional operations in the Caribbean region and throughout Europe, Asia and Australia. The Company is structured into three reportable segments – Paint Stores Group, Consumer Brands Group and Performance Coatings Group (collectively, the Reportable Segments) – and an Administrative function, which is representative of the way it is internally organized for assessing performance and making decisions regarding the allocation of resources. See Note 22 to the consolidated financial statements in Item 8 for further information on the Company’s Reportable Segments. Summary • Consolidated Net sales increased 2.1% in the year to $23.574 billion ◦ Net sales from stores in the Paint Stores Group open more than twelve calendar months increased 1.7% in the year • Diluted net income per share decreased 2.7% to $10.26 per share in the year compared to $10.55 per share in the full year 2024 ◦ Adjusted diluted net income per share increased 0.9% to $11.43 per share in the year compared to $11.33 per share in the full year 2024 • Generated Net operating cash of $3.452 billion, or 14.6% of Net sales in the year Outlook Sherwin-Williams delivered strong 2025 results driven by solid core performance and a focus on operational discipline despite continued demand choppiness. Full year Net sales grew to a record level, and gross profit and gross margin expanded. The Company continued to generate strong cash flow from operations, which was used for investment in capital expenditures, funding acquisitions and returning cash to shareholders through dividends and repurchases of common stock. Although the softer-for-longer demand environment is expected to continue in 2026, we have confidence in our differentiated strategy, Success by Design, that continues to deliver innovative and productive solutions for our customers. Significant opportunities exist for each business, and we will continue to support our growth strategy by executing initiatives within our enterprise priorities, including talent, simplification, digitization, supply chain responsiveness and sustainability. Within the Paint Stores and Consumer Brands groups, we anticipate continued economic pressures to impact customer buying behavior in 2026. Our investments in sales reps, training and digital tools, coupled with home builder relationships are expected to drive growth opportunities. The outlook for the Performance Coatings Group is varied by end market and region with an expectation that the core business remains flat, however, new account wins and favorable business sales mix should drive growth. At the business unit level, we expect modest growth in Automotive Refinish, Industrial Wood and General Industrial while Packaging sales are anticipated to be flattish. Coil sales are expected to be slightly negative

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The risks described below and in other documents we file from time to time with the SEC could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flow, liquidity or financial condition. Although the risks are organized by headings, and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. While we believe we have identified and discussed below the key risks affecting our business, there may be additional risks and uncertainties that are not presently known or that are not currently believed to be significant that may adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flow, liquidity or financial condition in the future. Readers should not interpret the disclosure of any risk factor to imply that the risk has not already materialized. ECONOMIC AND STRATEGIC RISKS Adverse changes in general business and economic conditions in the United States and worldwide have in the past adversely affected and may in the future adversely affect our results of operations, cash flow, liquidity or financial condition. We operate all over the world serving customers in more than 120 countries. Our business, operations and strategies are sensitive to global and regional business and economic conditions. Adverse changes in such conditions in the United States and worldwide have in the past impacted and may in the future reduce the demand for some of our products, adversely impact our ability to predict and meet any future changes in the demand for our products and impair the ability of those with whom we do business to satisfy their obligations to us, each of which could adversely affect our results of operations, cash flow, liquidity or financial condition. Changes in inflation rates, interest rates, tax rates, unemployment rates, labor costs, healthcare costs, recessionary conditions, geopolitical conditions, governmental policies, laws and regulations (including import and export requirements such as new or increased tariffs, sanctions, quotas or trade barriers), business disruptions due to cybersecurity incidents, terrorist activity, armed conflicts and wars (including the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine), public health crises, pandemics, outbreaks of disease, catastrophic events, adverse weather conditions or natural disasters (including those that may be related to climate change or otherwise), supply chain disruptions (including those caused by industry capacity constraints, labor shortages, raw material availability and transportation and logistics delays and constraints) and other economic factors have in the past and could in the future adversely affect demand for some of our products, our ability to predict and meet any future changes in the demand for our products, the availability, delivery or cost of raw materials, our ability to adequately staff and maintain operations at affected facilities and our results of operations, cash flow, liquidity or financial condition and that of our customers, vendors and suppliers. credit_strengths.text: Sherwin-Williams generates substantial operating cash flow, comfortably covering capital expenditures and leaving meaningful free cash flow for debt service and shareholder returns. This cash generation, supported by a portfolio of leading paint and coatings brands, provides a solid buffer against demand cyclicality and positions the company to fund growth initiatives without straining liquidity.

Operating margins exceed the sector median, reflecting pricing power and cost discipline in the company's Paint Stores and Performance Coatings segments. This profitability, combined with an interest coverage ratio above the sector median, underscores the company's ability to absorb higher borrowing costs and maintain financial flexibility through economic cycles.

key_risks.text: The company operates in over one hundred twenty countries and is exposed to adverse economic conditions, inflation, tariffs, and geopolitical conflicts, including the Russia-Ukraine war. These factors have historically reduced demand and pressured raw material costs, and management expects softer-for-longer demand in the coming year, which could impair cash flow and liquidity if conditions worsen.

Debt maturities are concentrated in the next few years, with a significant portion due in year two and additional amounts in years three through five. This schedule requires refinancing or repayment, and while the company has ample cash flow, a deterioration in credit markets or rising interest rates could increase refinancing costs and strain liquidity.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is strong, with operating income covering interest expense multiple times, well above the sector median. This cushion, combined with consistent operating cash flow, suggests the company can comfortably service its debt obligations even if earnings decline modestly, though coverage remains sensitive to profitability trends.

Free cash flow to debt is moderate, and net leverage sits above the sector median, indicating a somewhat higher debt burden relative to peers. However, the company's substantial cash flow and access to capital markets provide flexibility to manage maturities and maintain investment-grade credit metrics.

overall_credit_view.text: Sherwin-Williams exhibits an intermediate financial risk profile, with leverage above the sector median but strong cash flow and interest coverage. The company's diversified business and leading market positions support credit quality, though cyclical demand and geopolitical risks warrant monitoring. We view the credit as stable, with capacity to absorb moderate earnings volatility.

Shareholder distributions and acquisitions absorb a significant portion of free cash flow, limiting deleveraging potential. While this reflects confidence in cash generation, it also means debt reduction depends on earnings growth. We expect leverage to remain near current levels, and any large debt-funded acquisition or sustained demand weakness could pressure the credit profile.

credit_strengths.text: Sherwin-Williams 產生龐大營運現金流，足以輕鬆涵蓋資本支出，並留下可觀的自由現金流用於償債及股東回報。此現金產生能力，加上領先油漆及塗料品牌組合的支持，為需求週期性提供穩固緩衝，並使公司能夠在不對流動性造成壓力的情況下為增長計劃提供資金。
營運利潤率高於行業中位數，反映公司 Paint Stores 及 Performance Coatings 分部的定價能力及成本紀律。此盈利能力，加上高於行業中位數的利息覆蓋率，突顯公司有能力吸收較高借貸成本，並在經濟週期中維持財務靈活性。

key_risks.text: 公司於超過一百二十個國家營運，並面臨不利經濟狀況、通脹、關稅及地緣政治衝突（包括俄烏戰爭）的風險。該等因素歷來已減少需求並對原材料成本構成壓力，而管理層預期來年需求將持續偏軟，若情況惡化，可能損害現金流及流動性。
債務到期集中於未來數年，其中相當部分於第二年到期，第三至第五年亦有額外金額。此時間表需要再融資或償還，而儘管公司擁有充裕現金流，信貸市場惡化或利率上升可能增加再融資成本並對流動性構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率強勁，營運收入覆蓋利息支出多倍，遠高於行業中位數。此緩衝，加上穩定的營運現金流，表明即使盈利適度下降，公司仍能輕鬆償付債務責任，儘管覆蓋率仍對盈利能力趨勢敏感。
自由現金流對債務比率適中，而淨槓桿高於行業中位數，表明相對於同業債務負擔略高。然而，公司龐大的現金流及資本市場准入提供靈活性，以管理到期債務並維持投資級信貸指標。

overall_credit_view.text: Sherwin-Williams 展現中等財務風險狀況，槓桿高於行業中位數，但現金流及利息覆蓋率強勁。公司多元化業務及領先市場地位支持信貸質量，儘管週期性需求及地緣政治風險值得監察。我們認為信貸狀況穩定，具能力吸收適度盈利波動。
股東分派及收購吸收顯著部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿潛力。儘管此反映對現金產生能力的信心，亦意味債務減少取決於盈利增長。我們預期槓桿將維持於當前水平附近，而任何大型債務融資收購或持續需求疲弱可能對信貸狀況構成壓力。
